question.text: How many Fifth Circuit news announcements concerning the Judge Ada Brown misconduct proceeding will be dated November 1–12, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves by counting the entries displayed in the Fifth Circuit's News & Announcements listing filtered to November 2026 (https://www.ca5.uscourts.gov/news?month=11&year=2026) as of 5:00 p.m. Central Time (23:00 UTC) on November 13, 2026. Count each entry whose listing date is between November 1 and November 12, 2026 (inclusive) and which concerns the judicial misconduct proceeding involving U.S. District Judge Ada E. Brown — that is, the entry's title or linked document(s) name Judge Ada Brown, or reference Complaint No. 05-26-90177, Complaint No. 05-26-90196, or the Fifth Circuit Judicial Council's proceedings against her — and the entry counts even if the substance of the underlying document remains confidential or undisclosed. Entries unrelated to that matter (for example CM/ECF maintenance notices, vacancy announcements, proposed rule amendments, or oral-argument notices) are not counted, and where the same document appears in more than one entry it is counted once. Inclusion is determined by the date shown in the listing's date column, not by a date written into an entry's title. The resolved value is that count: for example, if the listing shows one qualifying entry dated November 3, 2026 and another dated November 12, 2026, the question resolves as 2; if it shows no qualifying entries, it resolves as 0.
question.fine_print: Entries whose listing date is November 13, 2026 or later are not counted, and an entry dated November 1–12, 2026 that is first displayed after the 5:00 p.m. Central Time snapshot on November 13, 2026 is not counted. If that listing or its month filter is unavailable, an archived copy of the listing or of the court's news pages (such as a Wayback Machine snapshot from November 13, 2026), or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the same postings, will be used to establish what was displayed.

[Texas Lawbook](https://texaslawbook.net/fifth-circuit-judicial-council-releases-report-on-ndtx-judge-ada-brown/); [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/us-law-week/judge-brown-emailed-sealed-court-papers-to-about-140-people); [Council statement](https://www.ca5.uscourts.gov/docs/6993a188-0839-418e-8574-f5268309a500/October%2019,%202026,%20Statement%20of%20the%20Fifth%20Circuit%20Judicial%20Council.pdf)

### 4. Base rates
- The 2026 listing has 21 entries in total, about 2 per month across all topics. Brown entries appear only from Oct 19 onward. [ca5 news](https://www.ca5.uscourts.gov/news)
- Earlier Brown orders were not posted as news items when they were issued: the Sept 21 exam order, the Sept 29 reassignment order and the Oct 16 interview order. They became public only in the Oct 19 batch, which was a reaction to Brown's leak.
- From Oct 19 to Oct 30 (12 days) there were 3 Brown entries. Each one followed a procedural step: the leak, the written-question order, and the no-show. In the 3 days since Oct 30 there have been 0.
- Section 360 confidentiality means a special committee report would normally not be made public. A Council order under Rule 24 is usually published only once action is final. In the Pauline Newman matter, the Council order came months after the committee steps.
- I found no exact precedent for how quickly a committee report follows a subject judge's refusal to cooperate.

### 5. Other forecasts
- None of the Kalshi markets provided match this question; they cover county judges, Watergate DOJ and similar topics. I found no Polymarket, Manifold or Metaculus market on the Brown proceeding.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The committee could file its report with the Council at any time, and the Council could then issue an order or statement. The Oct 20 order said a report would follow if Brown refused, and she has.
- Further triggers could include another leak or public statement by Brown, or a legal challenge by her that prompts a Council "transparency" release like the one on Oct 19.
- The Sept 29 order bars new case assignments for three months, until about Dec 29, so that expiry falls outside the window.
- The listing snapshot is taken Nov 13 at 23:00 UTC. Same-day posting has been the norm: listing dates have matched the dates in the titles.

## 4. Base rates
- **Posting pace:** The court posted 3 Brown entries between October 19 and 30. That is roughly one every 4 days, concentrated around specific triggers:
  - Brown's disclosure of the sealed papers (the October 19 statement)
  - a new order (October 20)
  - the scheduled appearance (October 30)
- **Before October 19:** No Brown entries were posted, even though substantive orders were issued on September 21 and 29 and October 1 and 16. The court went public in response to Brown's disclosures, so posting is not automatic.
- **Overall volume:** The listing is low-volume, with 21 items in 2026 through October (about 2 a month). That puts October's 6 items well above the norm.
- **Pace of reports in comparable cases:** In the Newman matter (Federal Circuit), the special committee's report came months after her non-cooperation, but that committee also issued interim orders. I found no case where a special committee report followed within two weeks of a missed interview.
- **Confidentiality:** Under 28 U.S.C. § 360, the committee's report itself is generally confidential. A report being filed might show up as a notice or statement rather than the report itself, or it might not be posted at all.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the Kalshi markets supplied (Harris and Bexar County Judge races, the DOJ Watergate investigation, news-story counts, and others) matches this question.
- I found no Polymarket, Manifold or Metaculus market, and no expert forecast, on Fifth Circuit postings about Brown.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **Committee report (timing unknown):** The October 20 order warned that if Brown did not answer, the committee "must proceed" to file its report with the Judicial Council. Both the October 27 written-answer deadline and the October 30 interview have passed, so filing the report is the next step. I found no public deadline for it.
- **Possible Council action:** The Council could act on the report (for example certifying disability, censure, or a request to retire) and might post a public order or statement.
- **Possible new orders:** The committee could issue further orders, such as on the psychiatric-exam non-compliance (the 30-day window from September 21 ran out around October 21), or on Brown's continued public disclosures.
- **Brown's own actions:** Further disclosures or public statements by Brown, or a legal challenge, could prompt another Council statement, as happened on October 19.
- **Existing reassignment:** The three-month reassignment order runs to about December 29, which is after the question window.
- **Listing quirks:** November 11 (Veterans Day) is a federal holiday. Late-dated entries would also matter: for example, if something posted on November 13 carries that date, it does not count.
